findings.passage: The first bill would create substantial new barriers and procedures for what used to be a relatively simple process of transferring firearms to a friend, relative, or neighbor. The new, complicated process could inadvertently turn law-abiding gun owners into criminals if they do not follow steps laid out in legislation.
findings.note: From his legislative update newsletter on the House floor passage of two gun bills (HF 8 and HF 9 in 2020). Describes the private-transfer background check bill as adding burdens for lawful owners.
subjects: check every gun buyer
private gun transfers

findings.passage: The second bill not only raises questions regarding the 2nd Amendment, but it also impacts due process rights.
findings.note: Same newsletter. On the extreme risk protection order bill: objects on Second Amendment and due-process grounds, including orders issued without the gun owner present, and concern for officers who would seize guns.
subjects: red-flag / extreme risk orders
Second Amendment general statement

findings.passage: Better legislation that I have signed as a co-author would strengthen laws we already have on the books including a bill that increases penalties for individuals that transfer a firearm to an individual that they know is legally barred from owning or possessing a firearm.
findings.note: Same newsletter. Says he co-authored a bill raising penalties for straw purchases and another to make sure people court-ordered to give up guns after abuse or stalking convictions actually do so.
subjects: straw purchases
removing guns from people barred from owning them

findings.passage: As a society, we need to continue to pursue measures that will keep our communities safe while ensuring that law-abiding Minnesotans’ 2nd Amendment rights are respected and upheld.
findings.note: Same newsletter, closing statement on gun rights and public safety.
